title: Handling Post-Op Fever, Swelling or Bleeding in Your Istanbul Hotel
seoTitle: Post-Op Emergency in an Istanbul Hotel: What to Do
metaDescription: Know red-flag post-op symptoms in Istanbul, who to call at 02:00 AM, why not to fly with fever, and how ER readmissions work financially.
quickAnswer: A post op emergency hotel istanbul plan starts before you leave the hospital. Mild soreness and predictable bruising are common after surgery, but high fever, soaking dressings, chest pain, or sudden leg swelling require immediate clinical assessment. Dial Türkiye's 112 emergency line for life-threatening symptoms, and contact your surgical team's 24/7 line first for urgent post-op concerns.

body.text: Recovering in an Istanbul hotel after surgery feels calmer when every contact number and decision threshold is already written down. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), we are an independent, client-paid, flat-fee advisory run by our two founders in Türkiye—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Itinerary of Türkiye does not provide clinical advice or emergency medical care, and no concierge or hotel desk should replace a licensed physician when symptoms change.
Which symptoms are normal recovery vs red-flag signs needing immediate surgeon or ER review?

Expected post-operative recovery typically involves localized aching, mild oozing that slows within 24 hours, symmetrical swelling, and fatigue controlled by prescribed medication. Red-flag signs—such as fever above 38°C, bright red bleeding soaking through dressings, chest pain, shortness of breath, foul wound discharge, or one-sided calf swelling—require urgent surgeon evaluation or emergency hospital care.

International public health guidance from the [CDC Yellow Book on Medical Tourism](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html) highlights infection, wound separation, and blood clots—including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism—as the primary post-surgical complications travellers must watch for. Because hotel rooms lack clinical monitoring, never wait until morning if symptoms worsen rapidly or feel disproportionate to what your discharge instructions described.

body.text: Who do you call first at 02:00 AM (clinic 24/7 line, hospital ER, 112, ITO local contact)?

Call Türkiye's national emergency number 112 immediately for life-threatening symptoms such as chest pain, breathing difficulty, fainting, or heavy uncontrolled bleeding. For urgent but stable surgical concerns—like a rising fever or dressing soakage—call your operating clinic's 24/7 nurse or surgeon line first, then notify your hotel front desk and Itinerary of Türkiye for transport logistics.

Per [GOV.UK Turkey Health Advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health), dialing 112 connects directly to ambulance services nationwide. The [Ireland Department of Foreign Affairs Türkiye Travel Advice](https://www.ireland.ie/en/dfa/overseas-travel/advice/turkiye/) also advises contacting 112 or your insurer directly rather than relying on ad-hoc third-party referrals to unfamiliar private clinics, where emergency billing can be unclear. Keep these essentials saved before surgery:

items: 112 National Emergency Line: State "English" clearly and hand the phone to the 24-hour hotel receptionist so they can give the exact Turkish street address and district.
Operating Surgeon / Hospital 24/7 Line: Your primary clinical contact who holds your operative report and anesthesia record.
Hospital Emergency Department Address: Saved in both Turkish and English for ambulance crews or private transfer drivers.
Travel Insurance Assistance Line: Keep your policy number and emergency claim line offline and printed.
Itinerary of Türkiye Local Contact: Available to coordinate hotel communication, companion support, and hospital transport logistics once clinical direction is set.

body.text: Why should you never board a flight while running a fever or active bleeding?

Never board an aircraft with an active fever, uncontrolled bleeding, or unassessed post-operative swelling. Aircraft cabins are pressurized to an altitude equivalent of 6,000–8,000 feet, which lowers oxygen levels, expands trapped internal gases, and—combined with immobility—sharply increases the risk of blood clots, wound separation, and in-flight medical emergencies far from surgical care.

The [UK Civil Aviation Authority Surgical Conditions Guidance](https://www.caa.co.uk/air-passengers/about-your-trip/health-and-medical/guidance-for-health-professionals/surgical-conditions/) warns that cabin pressure changes can stretch healing tissue and trigger hemorrhage after recent surgery, while the [IATA Aviation Medical Manual](https://www.iata.org/en/publications/medical-manual/) gives airlines authority to deny boarding to passengers showing signs of acute illness or unstable recovery. Even if you hold an earlier Fit-to-Fly letter, new symptoms invalidate that clearance—return to your operating surgeon for re-examination before travelling.
How do emergency hospital readmissions work financially?

Foreign visitors in Türkiye are not covered by Turkish public health insurance, and European EHIC or UK GHIC cards are not valid. Emergency departments treat everyone regardless of nationality, but you or your medical travel insurer will be billed for emergency triage, diagnostics, readmission nights, and any revision procedure unless explicitly included in your written clinic agreement.

Before paying any deposit for treatment, ask your chosen hospital to put its complication and readmission policy in writing. Clarify whether return ER visits, blood tests, imaging, IV antibiotics, or inpatient nights are covered by the clinic package or billed separately, and verify whether your specialist complication insurance covers planned surgery abroad—standard holiday policies usually exclude it. faq.q: Can a hotel doctor treat post-op surgical complications in Istanbul?
faq.a: No. A hotel call-out doctor does not have your operative notes, imaging, or surgical privileges. For surgical fever, bleeding, or wound changes, contact your operating surgeon's 24/7 line or go directly to a full-service hospital emergency department.

faq.q: Does 112 in Türkiye have English-speaking operators?
faq.a: English support on 112 can vary by shift and dispatch center. If you call 112 at night, say "English" clearly and ask your hotel's 24-hour front desk to speak with the operator to confirm your exact Istanbul address and room number.

faq.q: Will my standard travel insurance cover an emergency hospital readmission after elective surgery?
faq.a: Most standard holiday travel insurance policies exclude complications arising from planned elective surgery abroad. Check your policy wording carefully and consider dedicated medical tourism complication cover before travelling.

faq.q: What documents should I carry if I go to an Istanbul ER at night?
faq.a: Bring your passport, English operative report, discharge summary, current medication list, allergy list, and your operating hospital's direct phone number so ER physicians can coordinate immediately with your surgeon.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye arrange a nurse or give me advice on taking extra antibiotics?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye does not provide clinical advice, medication guidance, or emergency medical care. We coordinate hotel logistics, transport, and communication while your licensed medical team makes all clinical decisions.

faq.q: What if my surgeon says I cannot fly home tomorrow due to a fever?
faq.a: Follow your surgeon's medical instruction and postpone your flight immediately. Once your medical team sets a safe timeline, Itinerary of Türkiye can help coordinate your hotel extension and revised airport transfer.
